query: Given the framework we're calling off from already has its own performance regime built in, do we still need to separately set our own key performance indicators on this individual piece of work, or does the framework-level arrangement already cover that requirement for us?
expected_evidence: Whether the KPI duty attaches to the framework agreement itself or to each public contract awarded under it
Practical confirmation that a call-off contract is itself a public contract distinct from the framework for compliance purposes

query: When comparing tenders on things like price and quality, is there a legal requirement about how we go about deciding who wins, and do we have to tell people publicly who we've picked before the contract is actually signed?
expected_evidence: The contract must be awarded to the supplier submitting the most advantageous tender as assessed against award criteria that are set in a particular way: relating to the subject-matter, clear/measurable/specific, proportionate, and (if more than one) with their relative importance indicated (e.g. by weighting).

Before entering into the contract, the authority must publish a contract award notice, and before publishing it must give each supplier that submitted an assessed tender an assessment summary explaining how its tender (and the winning tender) was assessed.

query: One of our bidders is currently the subject of a central inquiry that could eventually see them barred from all public contracts, but that hasn't been decided yet and they're not on any published list. Do we have to wait for that process to finish before we can make our own call on this bidder, or can we act now within our own competition?
expected_evidence: A supplier is excluded/excludable either because the contracting authority itself considers a mandatory or discretionary exclusion ground applies, or (separately) because the supplier is on the centrally-kept debarment list; these are alternative, independent routes.

The central debarment-list process (investigation, report, and Minister's decision to add a supplier to the list) is a separate mechanism with its own timeline from an authority's own procurement-specific exclusion assessment, so an authority is not required to wait for the central process to conclude before forming its own view.

query: We awarded this contract a couple of years before the new Procurement Act rules came in, and it doesn't expire for a while yet. The company delivering it has just changed ownership, and the new structure looks like something that would count against them if they were bidding today. Does that ownership change give us a right to terminate the contract now, or are we limited to whatever termination grounds applied under the rules that were in force when we ran the original competition?
expected_evidence: Determine which legal regime governs an existing contract for termination purposes where the contract was awarded under PCR2015 before the Procurement Act 2023 commenced.

Identify the scope of the PCR2015 statutory/implied termination ground relating to supplier exclusion situations, in particular that it is tied to a situation existing at the time of contract award, and contrast this with the Procurement Act 2023's broader (but here inapplicable) post-award ground.
top10_citations: Procurement Act 2023 (Commencement No. 3 and Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2024 reg 6
Procurement Act 2023 (Commencement No. 3 and Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2024 reg 9

query: We ran a competitive tender for a specialist technical service, and neither of the two bids we got met our minimum quality bar, so neither could be taken forward. We still need this work done and don't want to just walk away from the requirement. Can we move to negotiating and awarding the contract directly to one of the bidders instead of starting the whole competition again, and if so, what do we need to do first?
expected_evidence: Identify the statutory route that allows a contracting authority to move to direct award after a competitive tendering procedure produced no suitable tenders, and its conditions.
Identify the procedural step (a transparency notice) required before the contracting authority can make the direct award.
top10_citations: Competitive Procedure with Negotiation | Procurement Journey

query: We have a below-threshold consultancy contract that we'd like to extend by six months and add a bit of extra scope, and the change would still leave it comfortably under the value where it would count as a full public contract. Do we need to justify this change against one of the Act's formal modification grounds, the same way we would for one of our larger contracts, or is there more flexibility for a contract of this size?
expected_evidence: Determine whether the Procurement Act 2023's formal modification-grounds regime applies to modifications of a below-threshold, non-convertible contract.
Identify the exception: if a modification would cause the contract to become a public contract (a 'convertible contract'), the formal modification rules would then apply to that modification.

query: We're looking at increasing the price on one of our contracts by around 12% and adding a new support tier, and we'd rather not run a whole new procurement for that. The contract was awarded a while back, before the procurement rules changed -- does that affect which modification rules apply, and would a change like this be allowed without a new competition?
expected_evidence: Confirm which modification regime governs changes made now to a contract that was awarded under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 before the Procurement Act 2023 commenced -- i.e. that the contract continues to be governed by the old regime's modification rules rather than switching to the Act's rules, correcting the contract manager's assumption.

Apply the applicable (2015 Regulations) modification test to the proposed ~12% price increase plus scope addition, including the relevant value threshold and the substantiality test, to determine whether a new procurement procedure would be required.
